ORAL ANSWERS TO QUESTIONS 
Indo Bangla Migrants Issue 
*661. SHRI K.B. KRISHANA MURTHY: Will the Minister of EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether India and Bangladesh have agreed to solve the migrants issue 
on the basis of their 1992 joint communique; 
(b) whether Dhaka has consistently and resolutely denied existence of its 
citizen on the Indian soil: 
(c) if so, whether India has presented detailed documentary proof in this 
regard; and 
(d) if so, Bangladesh Government's reaction thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE INTHE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRIVINODKHANNA):(a)to(d) AStatementisplacedontheTableoftheHouse. 
Statement 
(a) to (d) The Government has been concerned about large scale, illegal 
immigration from Bangladesh into India. The Government has been taking up 
the issue of illegal immigration with the Government of Bangladesh regularly. 
However, the Government of Bangladesh has been denying that large scale 
illegal immigration is taking place. 
2. During the visit of Mr. M. MorshedKhan, Foreign Minister of Bangladesh 
on February 13-15,2003, the issue of illegal immigration, including the need for 
tightening border control to prevent all kinds of illegal cross-border movement 
was discussed in detail. Further discussions were held during the Foreign 
Secretary level talks with Bangladesh on 29th April, 2003 and Director General-
level talks held between Border Security Force and Bangladesh Rifles on April 
27 to May 1,2003 in Dhaka. 
3. Following detailed discussions India and Bangladesh have committed to 
cooperate on the basis of the Joint Communique issued on 28th May, 1992 on 
1 

RAJYA S ABHA [8 May, 2003 ] 
the occasion of the visit of Her Excellency the Prime Minister of Bangladesh to 
India. Tighter border control is expected to lead to a decrease in the number of 
illegal migrants. 
4. Generally illegal immigrants do not possess travel or identity documents. 
However, when available evidence on illegal Bangladeshi nationals in India lias 
been shared, the Government of Bangladesh has taken back its nationals, after 
due verification of their nationality. 
SHRI K.B. KRISHNA MURTHY: Mr. Chairman, Sir, I would like to know fiom 
the hon. Minister whether the Government has taken a decision to repeal the 
IDMT Act, 1983. If so, has the Government all along felt that this was a major 
impediment in checking large-scale influx of migrants from the neighbouring 
countries? Part (b) of my question is: Has the Government of Assam expressed its 
apprehension that repealing of the Act would result in victimisation of minorities 
in the State? I would also like to know whether the Government is engaged in 
damage control of the situation arising out of the large-scale influx of migrants 
from Bangladesh. What are the reasons for not taking any preventive measures 
in the first place to check the entry of such illegal migrants into India? 
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI YASHWANT SINHA): 
Sir, so far as the first part of the question is concerned, it is correct that the 
Cabinet has decided for the repeal of this Act. The repealing Bill will come to 
Parliament very soon and I am sure, the hon. Members would have an opportunity 
of discussing it. So far as part (b) of his question is concerned, I very humbly 
submit that it would not be right to say that the Government has not taken any 
steps. The Government has been taking steps all along to prevent illegal migration 
from Bangladesh and we have reasons to believe that in recent years we have 
met with considerable success also. 
SHRI KB. KRISHNA MURTHY: Is it true that various Government 
agencies are harassing bona fide minorities, i.e. Muslims of India, on the

harassed by the Government agencies while checking illegal migrants from

(a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) and (c) Consequent to the grant of licenses for Cellular Mobile 
Telephone Sen ice (CMTS) to private op erators. Cellular Services were first 
started in the four Metro City Service Areas of Delhi, Mumbai. Kolkata and 
Chennai from August, 1995 onwards and thereafter in the Telecom Circle Service 
Areas beginning December. 1996. After adoption of New Telecom Policy-1999

(NTP-99) and shifting of the existing operators to the revenue sharing regime of 
NTP-99, additional licenses were granted to private operators: The cellular sen ice 
has been progressively rolled out by the private operators in the district 
headquarters and towns. According to information furnished by the Cellular 
Operators Association of India, about 1640 district headquarters and towns in 
various service areas across the countr y had been covered with the cellular 
service by March. 2003. Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd. started its cellular 
sen ices from February, 2001 in Delhi and Mumbai. Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited 
(BSNL) also started providing the servi ces in most parts of the country from 
October. 2002 and have so far covered about 1020 cities and towns with the 
cellular sen ice by March, 2003. Private operators coupled with the Government 
operators are expected to cover more and more places with the Cellular Senice 
over a period of lime. 
The terms and conditions of the Licence for CMTS require that in the Metro 
City Sen ice Areas an operator has to cover 90% of the Sendee Area within one 
\ car. and in the Telecom Circle Senice Areas, 10% of the District Headquarters 
within ons year and 50% of the District  Headquarters within three years. The 
licensee is also permitted to cover any other town in a district iniieu of the 
District Headquarter. The choice of District Headquarters/towns to be covered 
and further expansion beyond 50% District Headquarters/towns shall lie with 
ihe licensee depending on his business decision. There is no mandatory 
requirement for coverage of 100% of the districts as well as coverage of rural 
areas. 
Expansion for fresh start of CMTS in J&K. Assam and North East Telecom 
Circles was not permitted earlier on considerations of security. Tins was however 
permitted with effect from 21st August, 2002. Accordingly? BSNL has plans to 
launch its cellular senices in Jammu and Kashmir in the near future. BSNL also 
has plans to launch its cellular senices in Assam and North East Telecom Circles 
during the current financial year.

*671.  SHRIMOOLCHANDMEENA:  
           DR. T. SUBBARAMIREDDY:

(a) whether U.S. has imposed sanctions on Pakistan; 
36

Ob) if so. whether U.S. got a report that Pakistan has indulged in proliferation 
of nuclear technology; 
(c) whether U.S. has provided proof to the Pakistan on these charges; 
(d) if so. whether this would have a greater implication on India's security; 
and 
(e) if so. Government's reaction thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRIDIGVIJ AY SINGH): (a) to (c) The United States announced on 31 March. 
2003 that it had imposed non-proliferation penalties on Pakistan's Khan Research 
Laboratory (KRL) on 24 March 2003. The United States also imposed non-
proliferation sanctions on the North Korea entity Changgwang Sinyong 
Corporation (CSC) on the same day. 
2. The U.S. State Department clarified on 01 April. 2003 that the United 
States made a determination to impose penalties on both CSC and KRL as a 
result of a specific missile-related transfer from CSC to KRL. It further clarified 
that these sanctions did not pertain to any other activity, including nuclear-
related ones, and that the U.S. Administration had carefully reviewed the facts 
relating to the possible transfer of nuclear technology from Pakistan to North 
Korea, and decided that the facts do not warrant the imposition of sanctions 
under applicable U.S.laws. 
3. Proliferation activities in India's ne ighbourhood have implications for 
India's security. Government's defence preparedness fully takes into account 
these developments. 
4. Imposition of these sanctions substantiates Government's assessment 
regarding clandestine proliferation links between Pakistan and North Korea. 
Government welcomes all efforts to a ddress proliferation concerns regarding 
Pakistan.

Council would not be in conformity with the UN Charter; 
(b") if so, in what manner the UN Charter deals with such a situation if it 
actually happens; and 
(c) Governments views in this regard and the diplomatic steps it visualises 
to avoid such a situation and for maintaining universal peace? 
Ti IE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DIGVIJ AY SINGH): (a) to (c) Speaking in the specific context of Iraq, 
which was an issue colore the Security Council on March 10, the UN Secretary 
General said "If the US and others were to go outside the Council and take 
military action it would not be in conformity with the Charter". 
The Charter envisages use of force in case of self-defence or as authorised 
by the Security Council under Chapter VII. 
The Government had expressed its sense of deep anguish at the resort to 
military action in Iraq, which in its view lacked justification and was avoidable. 
Government has been in contact with other Governments on a more effective 
role by the UN in avoiding such situations and in strengthening international 
peace and security.

Nuclear power generation capacity 
4958. SHRIPREM CHAND GUPTA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased 
to state : 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have recently announced its intention 
to increase the nudearpower generation capacity from 2720 MW to 20,000 MW;

to the thermal power and the time-frame for its implementation? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE INTHE DEPARTMENT OF ATOMIC ENERGY 
(SHRI SATY ABRATA MOOKHERJEE): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) The present nuclear power generating capacity in the country is 2720 
MWe. This is scheduled to grow to 6680 MWeby December, 2008 progressively 
by completion of eight nuclear power reactor units (2x540 MWe at Tarapur, 
Maharashtra, 2x220 MWe at Kaiga, Kamataka, 2x1000 MWe at Kudankulam,

construction. More projects, subject to the availability of funds, are planned so 
as to reach a total nuclear power capacity of about 10,000 MWe by end of XI 
Plan. The aim is to reach a total nucl ear power generating capacity of about 
20,000 MWe by the year 2020. 
The capital cost per MWe of nudearpower plants is about Rs. 5 crore/MWe 
at 2001 -02 prices. In regard to coal thermal power plants it is about 20% lower 
than that of nuclear. However, the cost of generation from nuclear power plants 
is comparable to that of contemporary thermal power plants at locations about 
800 to 1000 km. from the coal pit-heads.

opportunities for Free/Open Source Software (OSS), more specially GNU/Linux

Government Institutions, localisation, R&D, inclusion of these in the Curricula/

Technology (DIT) maintains a stance of strict technology neutrality, platform

Multi-level marketing and direct selling of goods 
5003. SHRI ANIL SHARMA: Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, 
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether multi-level marketing, direct selling of goods and services is 
legal in India; 
(b) whether Government are aware that some multi-level marketing 
companies like JLI and Frontier Trading are unnecessarily being harassed by the 
authorities in different States including Delhi; 
(c) whether Government would take any preventive measures to ensure 
smooth functioning and to protect above companies against such harassment; 
(d) whether Government have received any representation from the above 
companies in this regard; and 
(e) if so, the action taken by Government thereon and by when all the 
States would be directed to stop such harassment? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI V. SREENIVASA 
PRASAD): (a) to (e) There is apparently no legal provision against marketing 
systems such as direct seli.ng/multi-level marketing of goods. However, some of 
these companies reportedly take deposits from agents in advance, complaints/ 
cases are lodged against them under the provisions of "Prize Chits and Money 
Circulation Scheme (Banning) Act, 1978". A few such cases are brought to our 
notice by some of these companies along  with their representation such as 
M/s. Frontier Trading, Mumbai, Cantos Marketing Private Ltd., Hyderabad etc. 
Legal provision in this regard has been examined. It was found that as long as 
these companies are selling goods in the normal manner just like any other form 
of marketing of goods. Government need not have to make any special measure 
for preventing the alleged harassment. The Government of India have written to 
the Governments of all States/Union Territories to distinguish between Companies 
dealing with activities coming strictly  under the purview of "Prize Chits and 
Money Circulation Scheme (Banning) Act, 1978 and those such as direct/ 
network/multi-level marketing dealing in the jurisdiction of goods so as to avoid 
harassment and commercial losses to bonafide investors.

Indo-Russian discussions on Iraq war 
5027. SHRI K. NATWAR SINGH : Will the Minister of EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state : 
(a) whether India and Russia had discussions regarding Iraq war and 
its impact on the situation in Afghanistan and the anti-terror campaign in the 
region. 
(b) if so. the points of discussions on these two important issues; 
(c) whether there is a similarity of approach between the two countries: 
and 
(d) if so, whether both the countries have agree to work together to 
impress the US to stop war against Iraq and start process of rebuilding of Iraq 
with full cooperation of Iraqi people? 
  THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRIDIGVIJAYSINGH):(a) Yes. 
(b) During the sixth meeting of the Indo-Russian Joint Working Group on 
Afghanistan held on 28 March,   2003 in Moscow, the two sides discussed. 
122 

[8 May, 2003] RAJYA S ABHA 
inter alia, the situation in Afghanistan and Iraq. The Minister of External Affairs and Mr. 
Igor lvanov, the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation, have also spoken 
to each other over telephone twice on 23 March and 24 April, 2003. The Iraq war was 
also discussed in these two telephonic conversations. The two sides shared their views 
about the military action against Iraq and expressed concern at the humanitarian 
situation in Iraq. India and Russia share the view that the military action against Iraq 
should not weaken the resolve of the international community to fight terrorism in 
Afghanistan and in the region. Discussions on Afghanistan included the progress in 
implementation of Bonn Agreement of December 2001, and coordination of various 
international efforts aimed at rehabilitation and reconstruction. India and Russia also 
discussed the threats to regional peace and stability from terrorist activity in the region, 
and efforts aimed at strengthening international mechanisms to fight against 
international terrorism. They expressed serious concern over the escalation of 
subversive and terrorist activity by the Taliban and Al Qaida remnants and others 
in Afghanistan and their efforts to regroup with support from the outside. 
(c) Yes. 
(d) India's position on these issues is reflected in the Resolution adopted by the 
Parliament of Indie on 8 and 9 April, 2003. 
Withdrawal of sanctions against civilian technology by U.S.A. 
5028. DR.T.SUBBARAMIREDDY: SHRIK. NATWAR 
SINGH: Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether American sanctions against India on civilian technology have 
been lifted; 
(b) if so, whether this was possible by follow-up paperwork done by the 
Political Advisor to the Prime Minister during his visit to Washington in the month 
of December, 2002; 
(c) if so, to what extent U.S. Government has finally cleared the US 
technology transfer to India; and 
(d) to what extent it would be helpful to India? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI 
DIGVIJAY SINGH): (a) In September 2001, the United States had lifted all sanctions 
against India imposed after the nuclear tests in May 1998. including 
123 

RAJYA SABHA [8 May, 2003] 
on export of dual use' technologies to India. However, the United States 
continues to maintain some restrictions on such exports on the basis of its 
domestic law and its obligations to the international non-proliferation regimes. 
(b) The subject of broader access for India to U.S. controlled 'dual use' 
goods and technologies has beeen an im portant element of bilateral dialogue 
with the United States at all levels, including during the National Security 
Adusor's visit to Washington D.C. in December 2002.

5030. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA MURTHY: Will the Minister of EXTERN AL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state :

have brightened with the Allies winning the war and the resultant change in the Iraqi 
regime;

and 
(c) whether India's ambivalent stand on the U.S. aggression on Iraq will come 
handy to leverage the recovery of Iraqi dues?

VINOD KHANNA) : (a) to (c) The Government of India and the Government of Iraq

placed on progressive institutionalization for providing timely and adequate credit

society to enable them to adopt modem technology and improve practices for increasing 
agriculture production and productivity. An amount of Rs. 7,36,570 crore is estimated as

through Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP). The scheme envisages that

money". For projects above Rs. 10 lakhs and upto Rs. 25 lakhs, rate of margin money

Removal of quantitative restrictions 
5096. SHRISURESH PACHOURI : Will the Minister of SMALL SCALE 
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have made any assessment regarding the role of Small 
Scale Industries reservations in the backdrop of the removal of quantitative restrictions; 
(b) if so, details thereof; and 
(c) how Government propose to safeguard the interests of Small Scale 
Industries? 
THE MINISTER OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES (DR C.P. THAKUR): (a) and 
(b) The role of Small Scale Industries (SSIs) reservation in the backdrop of removal of 
Quantitative Restrictions (QRs) is constantly being assessed/ monitored by the 
Government. While the removal of QRs on imports has implied greater integration of the 
Indian economy with the world, it is n ecessary that in the transition period 
employment, balanced regional growth and utilization of local resources by local 
entrepreneurs is promoted through support to SSIs. This is sought to be achieved 
through the policies and programmes for the Sector including the policy of reservation 
for exclusive manufacture in this sector. 
(c) To safeguard the interest of the Small Scale Industries, Government has 
already announced a Comprehensive Policy Package for SSIs on 30th August, 2000 in order 
to strengthen the SSI sector and enhance its competitiveness both 
172 

[8 May, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
domestically and globally. The package inter-alia provides for easier access to credit, 
availability of collateral free loans upto Rs. 25.00 lakhs, composite loans upto Rs. 25 
lakhs, capital subsidy for technology upgradation and improved infrastructure. 
SSI facing international competition 
5097 SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR : Will the Minister of SMALL SCALE 
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Small Scale Industries are facing the international competition 
after the removal of quantitative restrictions under the World Trade Organisation 
arrangement from April, 2001; 
(b) if so, whether it is fact that the Small Scale Industries are facing a tough 
competition with China, Singapore and other countries whose product of better quality 
are available at cheaper prices in the Indian market; and 
(c) if so, steps being taken by Government keeping in view the above facts? 
THE MINISTER OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES (DR. C.P. THAKUR): (a) and 
(b) Removal of Quantitative Restrictions have exposed the SSIs to greater competition 
with China, Singapore and other countries. However, the Small Scale Industries in 
India have shown resilience to withstand the impact of phasing out quantitative 
restrictions as is evident from their track record. 
(c) Government is constantly monitoring the impact of the removal of 
Quantitative Restrictions (QRs) on the economy including the Small Scale Industries 
(SSIs) in the country. Even after the removal of QRs, protection to the industries is 
available in the form of raising custom duties upto the bound levels, imposing anti-
dumping duties and taking safeguard measures in case of surge in imports. Government 
has also put in place several measures to strengthen the small scale industries to make 
them globally competitive. These include special focus on areas such as technology 
upgradation, infrastructure assistance through cluster approach, timely availability of 
credit, adoption of modem management practices, use of electronic infrastructure and 
other IT applications to face the emerging challenges of trade liberalization.

THE CONSTITUTION (NINETY-FIFTH AMENDMENT) BILL, 2003 
AND 
THE CONSTITUTION (NINETY-SIXTH AMENDMENT) BILL. 2003 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE A ND COMPANY AFFAIRS (SHRI 
JASWANT SINGH): Mr. Chairman, Sir, I move: 
* That the Bill further to amend the Constitution of India as 
passed by Lok Sabha be taken into consideration." 
This Constitution (Ninety-Fifth Amendment) Bill, 2003, seeks to 
provide for tax on services as a separate entry for taxation and for related 
Central legislation to govern various modalities in that respect. 
Sir, in most developed countries, goods and services are traded and 
taxed together. Taxation of services in India was started through the Union 
Budget, 1994-95, when it was levied, with effect from July 1, 1994, on 
stockbrokers, general insurance and tele phone services; if I am not mistaken, 
the hon. Leader of the Oppo sition was the author of th is initiative then. The 
power to levy tax on services is, howeve r, not specifically mentioned either in 
the Union List or the Stat e List in the Seventh Schedule of Constitution; Entry 
97 of the Union List, which gives power to the Centre for levy and collection of 
"any tax not mentioned in ei ther of List II and List III". At present, therefore, 
Parliament has the power to levy and collect tax on services only as a residual 
taxation matter. In exer cise of this power, the Central Government has 
periodically taxed selected services. 
Sir, the role of this sector in t he economy being significant - with the 
service sector accounting for 48-plus per cent of the GDP - and on the basis of 
deliberations between the State Gove rnments and the Central Government, 
also in accordance with the views of the recommendations of Expert 
Committees, it has been proposed to suitably amend the Constitution: (i) to 
introduce a new entry (Entry No. 92C- Taxes on services) in the Union List 
(List I) of the Seventh Schedule of the Co nstitution; (ii) to insert a new article 
268A in the Constitution to provide for levy of tax on services by the Union and 
collection and appropriation of the pr oceeds thereof by the Union and the 
States in accordance with principles to be laid down by a new law to be 
enacted by Parliament; (iii) after the proposed 
205 

RAJYA SABHA [8 May, 2003)  
amendments to the Constitution are effe cted, to enact a suitable Central 
legislation to provide for all necessary modalities, including levy of the tax on 
services by the Union Government and collection and appropriation of the 
proceeds of this tax, up to the prescribed ad valorem limits, by the Union and 
the States, respectively. 
After this proposed amendment to the Constitution is considered 
and passed by Parliament and ratified by the State Legislatures, suitable 
Central legislation will be enacted to provide for all necessary modalities, 
including collection and appropriation of the proceeds of taxes on services by 
the Union and the States, respectively. 
Sir, this proposed amendment will facilitate reforms in the Domestic 
Trade System and, most importantly, it will widen the tax base of the States, 
as and when this Bill, this taxation measure, begins to be effectively 
implemented. 
Sir, I must also add here that this is only an enabling provision that 
through the Constitution, we have the le vying and collecting of service tax by 
the Centre and the States. This woul d, significantly, increase the revenue 
receipt collection of the States. And,  it is only after this Constitution 
Amendment is adopted, we will be bringing forth a Bill as early as possible. We 
would have brought it in this Session itself, but for the delay that has taken 
place. And we will have a legislation on service tax proper, in which we will 
consider fully whether the tax is to be shared or the services are to be shared, 
and it will be entirely possible because it is not practical for the Centre to tax all 
the services; and there are some services for which it will be more practical to 
leave them entirely in the care of the States. Now, these are the details, which 
will be taken up when this Bill proper for services tax comes up. This is only an 
enabling provision. I thought I should emphasise this. 
The question was proposed. 
DR. MANMOHAN SINGH (Assam): Sir, I rise to support this Bill. The 
fiscal system of our country is under great strain. In fact, the fiscal deficit of the 
Centre and the States, which now exce eds nearly 11 per cent of our Gross 
Domestic Product, is among the highest in the developing countries. Efforts 
have been made from time to time to tackle the fiscal malaise particularly the 
control of expenditure. Promises have been made, but, unfortunately, in 
particular, with regard to expenditure co ntrol, the last five years have seen 
retrogression, not progression.  In the same way, in the 
206 

[8 May, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
last decade, a good deal of attenti on has been paid to reforming the tax 
system of our country. But the sad rea lity is that the tax:GDP ratio in our 
country today is 2:2.5 per cent of the GDP lower than what it was some 10-12 
years ago. Therefore, we have to pond er over the conseq uences of the way 
the fiscal system of India is being ma naged. Emphasis has to be laid both on 
expenditure control and tax reform, with a tighter tax administration. These are 
the obvious routes to bring the fiscal system of our country into a proper 
shape. 
It was in this context that when I was the Finance Minister, we began 
the practice of taxing the services that the hon. Minister haa mentioned. It was 
in the Budget of 1994-95 that, for the first time, services were brought within 
the purview of the Union taxation. There is no explicit En try in Schedule VII, 
either in the Union List or  in the State List, which mentions the taxation of 
services. Therefore, at that time, we took advantage of Entry 97 of the Union 
List, which enables the Union Govern ment to tax items, which are not 
mentioned otherwise in either the Unio n List or the State List. This is, 
obviously, not a very satisfactory arran gement and, therefor e, the decision of 
the Government to get the Constitution amended to make an explicit provision 
for the taxation of services, and giving the Union the right to legislate about the 
basic principle on which this taxation should be based, is a sound one. 
[THE DEPUTY CHAIRMAN in the Chair.] 
Also, the provision in the Constitutional amendment that the 
collection and appropriation will be the responsibility of both the Government 
of India and the States, in a manner to be prescribed by Parliament by law, I 
think, is also a sound provision. 
Madam, there are, however, two or three things that I would like to 
mention. India has premat urely graduated to the stat us of a service economy. 
In the history of the developing countries,  or, in the history of the developed 
countries, the stage when a country reaches  a position where 50 per cent of 
its GDP accounted for services, comes no rmally, much after industrialisation 
has progressed. Unfortunately, in our country, the pace of industrial growth 
has not been very rapid, and we have prematurely graduated to a service 
economy; the services today account for nearly 50 per cent of our GDP. The 
reasons for this are numerous. I do not wish to go into those reasons. But 
given the weight of services in our nation al economy,  it is entirely appropriate 
that services ought to be brought

to Parliament with a fresh legislation which will lay down the broad principles 
on which services ought to be taxed in our country. I would respectfully submit 
to him that adequate preparation should  be made for this purpose. The Bill, 
when it is ready, should be made available for discussion by the public. Those 
who are affected by the provisions of th is Bill, they should be consulted; and

that will add to the revenues of t he States. Having a service tax on the 
Concurrent List has certain difficulties, as I attempted to share my views with 
the hon. Member. For example, if we have the right to levy tax on the States, in

practical difficulties in this regard and that is why the entire arrangement of the 
Constitution has been structured, as the eminent jurist, Mr. Nariman, pointed 
out, in a particular manner. For example, this right were available with the 
States - and, say, it is the right of insu rance - State "A" might levy 10 per cent

non-existent and some States  might benefit by the exis tence of a wide variety

therefore, mandatory and th e duty of the Union Government to arrive at as 
uniformed structure of taxation as possi ble. Therefore, when introducing the

some unforeseen reason, the 2001 Census is delayed; the figures are 
delayed, would we run into a situati on where we are caught between two 
stools, as the phrase is used, so that we have no figures available as to how 
the next set of elections are to be conducted? That, I am afraid, may not be 
necessary because under the Constitution itself, they had visualised the 
situation of this kind happening, and both in article 82 relating to the 
composition of the seats for the House of  People, that is, the Lok Sabha, and 
in article 170 for the composition of s eats of the Legislative Assemblies, the 
second proviso to article 170 (3), and the second proviso to article 82 (3) itself 
clarifies this. I will just read out the proviso: "Provided further that such 
readjustment shall take effect from such  date on which the President may, by 
order, specify. And until such readjustment takes effect, any election to the 
Legislative Assembly may be held on bas is of the territorial constituencies 
existing before such readjustment.* In fact, whenever we read this Constitution 
document, we appreciate those who drafted this document because almost 
every conceivable contingency has been taken care of at the time of the 
drafting of the original text. So, the orig inal Constitution was so drafted that a 
contingency of this kind, where the ne xt figures are not available, we don't 
jump into a situation of vacuum where we  have no figures available. That is a 
situation where article 170 and article 82 have a proviso which deals with the 
situation. Therefore, I do  hope that such a situation may not arise. Madam, 
with regard to the number of consti tuencies, the hon. Member, and my 
colleague had raised this question, and some Members had also raised this 
question about reservation of constituencies for the Scheduled Castes and the 
Scheduled Tribes voters and electorates.  A conscious decision has already 
been taken

figure; in proportion to that figure, the reservation of constituencies would take 
place. With these words, I commend to this House that this amendment to the

SHRIMATIN.P DURGA : 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether in an International symposium on plant pathogens held at ierabad

known fungicides and pesticides, etc.;

Statement 
(a) In a National Symposium (not International) on "Plant Pathogens crsity in

plant pathogens under in vitro conditions. However, no fungicides were

MANOHAR JOSffl): (a) to (e) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (e) Guidelines have been issued by the Cabinet Secretariat in December 1999 
regarding clearance for study/research schemes involving foreigners/foreign collaboration 
from security/sensitivity angle and by the Ministry of Home Affairs in September 2000 
regarding security clearance for holding international conferences/seminars/workshop 
etc. in India. The guidelines which have been issued by Ministry of Human Resource 
Development on 31st January 2003 relate to the procedure to be observed by Central 
Universities to enter into an MoU with foreign Universities/Institutes with prior 
clearance from Ministry of Human Resource Development. Similarly, guidelines have 
been issued to State Universities and Deemed Universities permitting them to enter into 
MoU with foreign Universities/Institutes with prior clearance from State Governments 
and University Grants Commission respectively.

scholars/students coming to India or their academic activities. The guidelines lay 
down the procedure for obtaining approval of competent authority keeping

THE MTMSTEROF STATE OFTHE MINISTRY OFFOOD PROCESSING

Statement 
(a) and (b) A Group of Ministers (GOM) has been constituted by the 
Government to propose legislative and other changes for preparing a Modem 
Integrated Food Law and related regulations. It is proposed to converge and 
modernize the existing laws and to bring about a single statute for regulation of food 
products. This law is expected to take into account the international scenario and the 
modem developments so as to create an enabling environment for compliance 
by the industry. 
(c) The Government has taken following policy initiatives for rapid growth of 
the food processing sector. 
1. A draft National Food Processing Policy has been framed and Group of 
Ministers (GOM) has been entrusted with the responsibility of approving the draft 
Policy. The proposed draft policy aims at creating an enabling environment through 
harmonization and simplification of food laws, rationalization of tax structure, 
creation of infrastructural facilities, development of human skills and expertise 
through Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDPs) etc. and special 
consideration in development of policy and plants for North Eastern Region. 
2. The central excise duty has been brought down from 16% to 0% on 
processsed fruits and vegetable products, 16% to 8% on consumer products like 
biscuits etc. and 32 to 24% on aerated soft drinks. 
3. In order to encourage setting up of more units in this sector, foreign direct 
investment in this sector has been brought under automatic route with certain 
conditions. 
4. Ministry of Food Processing Industries under its Plan Schemes provides 
financial assistance by way of grant-in-aid for: 
(i)    Technology Upgradation, Establishment/Modernization of Food 
Processing Industries 
(ii)    Human Resource Development 
(iii)    Quality Assurance and Research & Development 
(iv)    Strengthening of Institutions

Availability of water for agricultural production 
5133. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:Will the Minister of AGRICULTURAL 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the country has been experiencing poor rains 
during the last five years; 
(b) if so, the man made reasons therefore and the rain prospects this year; 
(c) whether Government have assessed the impact of poor rains on rural 
income and its purchasing power;. 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the steps being taken to ensure sufficient availability of water for 
agricultural production? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI 
HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and (b) The monsoon rains in the 
76 

[9 May, 2003] RAJYASABHA 
country have been less than Long Period Average (LPA) in four out of past five years. 
According to the revised classification of monsoon rainfall for the country as a whole, 
the rainfall was below normal (90 to 97% of LPA) inl 999,2000 &2001 and in drought 
category (less than 90% of LPA) in 2002. In 1998, the monsoon 
rainfall was above normal (103 to 110% of LPA). 
There is no evidence of long term trend in South-west monsoon rainfall 
which can be attributed to man-made reasons. The inter annual fluctuations are with in 
the natural variability of monsoon phenomenon. 
Based upon the newly adopted 8-Parameter Power Regression Model, India 
Meteorological Department (IMD's) long range forecast for the 2003 Southwest 
Monsoon Season (June-September) is that the rainfall for the country as a whole is 
likely to be 96% of the LPA with a model error of ±5%. 
(c) and (d) The impact of poor rains on rural income and its purchasing power 
is mainly due to adverse impact on agricultural production. However, the temporal and 
spatial distribution of rainfall is equally important. During 2001, monsoon rainfall 
was 8% less than LPA for the country as a whole, nevertheless, the agricultural 
production was an all time high for foodgrains. During 2002, the monsoon rainfall 
was abnormally low, especially in July, which is the most agriculturally active 
month; this led to sharp decline in agricultural production in respect of most of the 
crops. The resultant adverse impact on farm economy was assessed and accordingly 
drought relief allowance over and above the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for 
important rabi and kharif crops was announced. 
(e) In order to augment the availability of water in country for irrigation and other 
uses and for their efficient use, a large number of dams have been constructed thereby 
creating 177 billion cubic metre (BCM) of storage capacity. Another 75 BCM of 
storage will be created on completion of dams which are under various stages of 
construction. Proposals to take up additional dams to create a live storage capacity of 
132 BCM are also under formulation/consideration. To accelerate creation of 
irrigation of potential by early completion of ongoing schemes, Government has 
launched Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme (AIBP). Central Ground Water 
Board has also taken up a Central Sector Scheme on "Studies of Recharge to Ground 
Water" on pilot basis. Assistance is also being extended to State Government under 
Command Area Development (CAD) Programme for bridging the gap between 
potential created and utilized. For meeting future requirements of water, as a long 
term measure, National Water Development Agency have formulated National 
Perspective Plan for water resources development which envisages interlinking 
various Peninsular rivers 
77 

RAJYA SABHA [9 May, 2003J 
and Himalayan rivers for transfer of water from surplus basins to water deficit basins. 
The Government is conscious of the need to ensure for efficient use of water for 
agriculture, which in essence is an integral part of sustainable development of 
agriculture as enshrined in the National Policy on Agriculture. Efforts aimed at 
diversification of agriculture constitute an important initiative in this direction, because this 
would facilitate the much-needed shift from the rice-wheat system in areas suffering 
from the stress on ground water resources. Further, priority is accorded to the holistic 
and sustainable development of semi-arid rainfed areas through integrated watershed 
development approach in which the construction of micro irrigation facilities like water 
harvesting structures, village ponds, check dams, etc. are promoted.

5 Million Standard Cubic Meter Per Day (MMSCMD) of gas for the production of 
1,30,000 TPA Ethylene and the Oil & Natural Gas Commission (ONGQ would supply 1.35 
MMSCMD for the rernaining 70,000 TPA of Ethylene. However, it is now estimated that 
with 1.35 MMSCMD of gas available from ONGC, it would be possible to produce only 
28,000 TPA of Ethylene in the first 5 years and for the remaining 10 years, it would be 
sufficient to produce 15,000 TPA of Ethylene only. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural 
Gas have identified Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) for supply of LPG to make up for the 
shortfall in the supply of gas. 
With the passage of time, the price of gas has increased and subsidy to the oil 
companies will have to be given to provide gas at a concessional fixed rate of Rs. 600 per 
thousand cu. Meters of gas over a period of 15 years for the project, as decided by the 
Cabinet in 1994. Action has been initiated for the expeditious resolution of the issue of 
funds required for subsidy for the Assam Gas Cracker Project. 
The cost of the project is estimated at Rs. 3600 crore. On fmalization of the 
Feedstock Supply Agreement(s) and acquisition of land, the project authorities expect

Liter cy rate 
5185.SHRI SURESH PACHOURI: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that so far literacy rates are concerned there are wide 
inter and intra State differences; 
(b) if so, the details thereof with literacy rates among male and female 
separately; and 
(c) the steps taken by Government to improve the situation so far female 
literacy rates, especially in Northern States are concerned ? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIASHOK PRADHAN): (a) and (b) A statement giving 
State-wise break up of literacy rates of males and females in 1991 and 2001 is 
annexed. (See below). 
(c) The steps taken by Government under various Schemes to improve 
female literacy rates are as follows: 
(1) Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan 
A new Scheme of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) has been launched to 
implement Universalization of Elementary Education. The goals of SSA are as 
follows: 
• All children in school/Education Guarantee Scheme center, Alternate 
school, back to school camp by 2003. 
• All children complete five years primary education by 2007. 
• All children complete eight years of schooling by 2010. 
• Focus on Elementary Education of satisfactory quality with emphasis 
on education for life. 
• Bridge all gender and social gaps at primary stage by 2007 and at 
Elementary Education level by 2010. 
• Universal retention by 2010. 
122 

[9 May, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
In addition, some of the special interventions included for the girl child are: 
• Intervention for early Childhood Care and Education. 
• School/EGS like alternative facility to be set up within one kilometre of all 
habitations. 
• Upgradation of EGS to regular schools. 
• Special mainstreaming camps for out-of-school girls/SC/ST children 
under the alternative and innovative Education Component. 
• Provision of process based community participation with a focus on the 
participation of women and SC/ST. 
• Provision of contact specific innovative intervention for girls' 
education and education of SC/ST children upto Rs. SO lakhs in a district 
in a particular year in which the ceiling for each intervention is Rs. 15 
lakhs. 
• Mid-day meal programme. 
• Incentives like uniforms and scholarships to be funded from State Plan 
only. 
• Adequate Teaching Learning Equipment for all Primary and Upper 
Primary schools. 
• Atleast 50% of the teachers to be appointed have to be women. 
• Special teaching support as per need. 
• Using Community Teachers. 
• Provision of free textbooks to all girl/SC/ST children at primary and upper 
primary level with an upper ceiling of Rs. 150/- per child. 
(2) Mahila Samakhya 
Manila Samakhya Programme has been in operation since 1989. It is a 
women's empowerment project and endeavours to create an environment for women 
to seek knowledge and information in order to make informed choices. The 
principal strategy is to organize women into collectives called Mahila Sanghas to 
identify their needs and evolve collective ways to deal with their problems. 
Currently, the Mahila Samakhya programme is operating in 60 districts 
covering more than 9000 villages in 10 states of Uttar Pradesh, Kamataka, Gujarat, 
Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Bihar, Madh ya Pradesh, Assam, Jharkhand and 
Uttaranchal. 
(3) National Literacy Mission 
Under National Literacy Mission (NLM) focus is given on female literacy. 
Special innovative projects are being taken up to raise the level of female literacy in 
low female literacy areas. Special efforts are being made to target female 
Panchayati Raj functionaries and make them literate.

Schemes to check crimes in trains 
†5237. PROF. R.B. S. VARMA: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether Government have formulated any special scheme to check the 
crime taking place in trains; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(SHRIBANDARU DATTATRAYA): (a) and (b) "Policing" being a State subject, the 
security of passengers and their belongings in the running trains is the constitutional 
responsibility to the Government Railway Police (GRP), which functions under the 
control of the State Government concerned. The cases of crime on Railways are 
reported to, registered and investigated by the Government Railway Police. 
The Railway Administration coordinates with the GRP so that the security of the 
passengers may be ensured. Though the responsibility to curb these incidents lies 
with the State Governments, the railways also taken the following steps to supplement 
the efforts of the State Governments. 
1. Anti-social elements are removed from Railway premises and trains by RPF. 
2. Coach Attendants/TTEs keep proper watch on the passengers entering/ 
detraining from the coaches. 
3. Coaches are locked during their run especially during night hours. 
4. Wherever the State Government wants to establish mobile post in the running 
trains, necessary facilities like accommodation etc. are provided. 
5. FIR forms are mac's available with the Train Guards/Station Masters/ RPF to 
facilitate the travelling public to lodge their reports immediately. 
6. RPF Assistance Posts are provided at important stations to assist 
passengers in lodging FIRs with Government Railway Police.

analyze the crime position with a view to taking suitable preventive measures.

TECHNOLOGY IN THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY (SHRI

out of these, four have been supported by the Department of Biotechnology.

Performance of hockey and football players 
5261. SHRI SHANKAR ROY CHOWDHURY: Will the Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any formalised structure exists to assess the performance of young 
football and hockey players during the National trophy events like the Subroto Cup 
and Junior Nehru Cup; 
(b) the arrangements for proper follow-up and training programmes 
thereafter for the players; and 
(c) whether there are plans to extend astro-turf facilities for coaching and training 
of junior hockey players at Kolkata, other than theexisting one at Salt Lake Stadium ? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI VJKRAM 
VERMA) : (a) and (b) Yes Sir, Subroto Mukherjee Sports Education Society 
(SMSES) has set up a formalised structure which not only conducts the tournament 
but also ensures follow-up of selected players with regard to their recruitment in IAF, 
award of Government scholarship by Netaji Subhash Institute of Sports (NSNIS), 
Patiala/Sports Authority of India (SAT) and spotting of talents by other agencies. The 
Society constitutes a three member Selection Committee to assess the young 
footballers comprising of representative of All India Football Federation, a 
representative of Sports Authority of India, and a representative of Subroto Mukherjee 
Sports Education Society. The Selection Committee selects outstanding players from 
junior and sub-junior players and forwards their names to NIS, Patiala. The Society 
also awards scholarship @ Rs.2500/- per annum to selected players. 
As regards Hockey, it is stated that there is no such tournament known as Junior 
Nehru Cup. However, Jawaharlal Nehru Hockey Tournament Society (JNHTS) 
organises 5 tournaments every year in Delhi viz; Sub-junior (Boys under-15), Junior 
(Boys under-17), Girls (under-17), Championship Colleges Hockey Tournament and 
Main Open Tournament for meii: JNHTS also has a formalised structure to assess the 
performance of players during the junior hockey tournaments. For this purpose, 
there is a Committee headed by an Olympian, representative from Sports Authority of 
India (SAI), representative from Indian Hockey Federation (IHF) and two nominees 
from JNHTS. 
Arrangements for proper follow-up and training of the sportspersons are done by 
the respective societies. The talent identified from these tournaments are eligible for 
national level scholarships under the Scholarship Scheme of the Government of India. 
Scholarship is given subject to the condition that identified talent is not under any 
approved training scheme of SAI or State Government. As such, the identified talent is 
also taken by SAI for training under its various schemes. 
(c) No, Sir.

Foreign Direct Investment in Electronic Media 
SHRI   MANOJ   BHATTACHARYA  (West  Bengal):   Sir,   I  call  the 
attention of the hon. Minister of Information and Broadcasting to the issue 
225 

RAJYA SABHA [9 May, 2003] 
of foreign direct investment in electronic media in particular.   Thank you. 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION 
AND BROADCASTING (SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD): Sir. I will present 
before the hon. House a brief statement about the entire gamut. The hon. 
Members have drawn my attention to their concerns over the entry of foreign 
companies in the electronic media in our country. Let me inform this hon. 
House about the decision taken by the Government. 
I would like to make a brief statement on the existing regime as well 
as the present status in respect of various service segments. 
1. Cable Network Service 
As per the provisions of the Cable Television Network (Regulation) 
Act, 1995, no licence is required but a 'person' is required to be registered as a 
cable operator with the Head Postmaster of a Head Post Office of the area 
concerned. A person means, - (i) a n individual who is a citizen of India; (ii) an 
association of individuals or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not, 
whose members are citizens of India; and (iii) a company in which not less 
than 51 per cent of the paid-up share capital is held by the citizens of India. 
2. Direct-to-Home Broadcasting Service (DTH) 
The Government took a decision to start the DTH in the country in 
November 2000 after the Group of Ministers had deliberated and considered 
all the issues connected thereto at length. Detailed guidelines for starting DTH 
service were issued by the Government on 15th March, 2001. 
So far, only three applications for starting DTH broadcasting service 
have been received.  They are from, 
i) Space T.V. Private Limited 
ii) A.S.C. Enterprises Limited, and 
iii) Essel Shyam Communication Limited. 
226 

[9 May, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
The eligibility criteria under the DTH are: 
(a) Applicant-company to be an Indian company registered 
under the Companies Act, 1956. 
(b) Total foreign equity holding (including FDI/NRI/OCB/FII) in 
the uplinking company not to exceed 49 per cent. 
(c) Within the foreign equity, the FDI component not to exceed 
20 per cent. The quantum represented by the proportion of 
the paid-up equity share capital to the total issued equity 
capital of the Indian promoter company, held or controlled 
by the foreign investors through FDI/NRI/OCB investments 
shall form part of the abovesaid FDI limit of 20 per cent. 
All these applications are under process. 
3. Uplinking Policy 
I am reading out a gist of the policy module for uplinking.   These are: 
(a) For setting up of uplinking hub/teleports, the company has 
to be incorporated in India and equity holding including 
NRI/OCB/PIO not to exceed 49 per cent. 
(b) For uplinking a T.V. channel, no restrictions on ownership, 
equity structure or management control of the channel 
which is aimed at Indian viewership. 
(c) For uplinking by news agencies, th3 company has to be 
incorporated in India and accredited by PIB. One hundred 
per cent owned by Indians with Indian management control. 
[THE DEPUTY CHAIRMAN in the Chair] 
The Government have announced fresh guidelines in March, 2003 
227 

RAJYA SABHA [9 May, 2003] 
for uplinking of foreign owned news channels. The guidelines, inter alia, permit 
foreign equity holding in the applicant-company up to 26 per cent of the total 
paid-up capital and require the company to be registered in India, under the 
Companies Act, 1956 and the majority of Directors, CEO and News Editors to 
be Resident Indians. The permission for usage of facilities/infrastructure for 
live news/footage collection and transmission, irrespective of the technology 
used, will be available to only those channels which are uplinked from India 
and the channel/company has to ensure that its news and current affairs 
content providers, if any, are accredited with the Press Information Bureau. 
Under the extant policy for uplinking, 31 companies have been 
permitted to uplink 88 channels, 20 companies permitted to set up 22 teleports 
and a news agency permitted for news-gathering and distribution. 
4. F.M. Broadcasting 
Twenty per cent portfolio investment by NRIs, F.I.Is and Persons of 
Indian Origin (Pol) and Overseas Corporate Bodies (OCBs) has been 
permitted in private F.M. radio. F.D.I, is not permitted. Companies should be 
registered under the Companies Act, 1956. 
In the four metros of Chennai, Delhi, Kolkata and Mumbai, 14 private 
F.M. stations have been operationalised. In the non-metros, 8 private F.M. 
stations have been operationalised, bringing the total number of 
operationalised channels (both metro and non-metro) to 22.

(iv)        Cable Service Network 
Under the provisions of the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) 
Act, 1995, a person has to be registered with the Head Post Office of the area 
of operation concerned. Such a person shall be a citizen of India, and in the 
case of a company, not less than 51 per cent of the paid-up share capital 
should be held by the citizens of India. The programme and advertisement to 
be transmitted/retransmitted shall be strictly in conformity with the prescribed 
Codes, laid down thereat. Every cable operator is also required to maintain a 
register indicating therein the programmes transmitted or retransmitted during 
a month, for a period of one year after the same. The power to prohibit 
transmission/retransmission of programmes in public interest has been vested 
in the authorised officers notified by the Central or the State Governments. 
The Central Government has also been empowered to prohibit the operation 
of the cable T.V. network where it thinks necessary or expedient so to do in 
the interest of the sovereignty, integrity and security of India, etc.

licensee shall stop forthwith transmission of T.V. channels or any

IV Uplinking  
Now, before I speak on the Uplinking Policy Guidelines, I would like 
to inform the hon. Members that it has been the constant endeavour of the 
Government of India to closely monitor and review the policy at periodic 
intervals, so as to keep pace with the changing economic scenario and 
globalisation, while simultaneously balancing he need for taking care of the 
security concerns. 
Recently, there was a felt need for restrictions of foreign equity in 
respect of foreign owned and controlled TV news channels. It was perceived 
that (i) there could be a threat to the security of the State in times of external 
aggression, by furthering the interests of the enemy; (ii) it may jeopardize the 
internal security as well as law and order, by encouraging communal strife and 
dissensions; (ii) may exercise an unhealthy influence on our democratic 
processes to suit vested foreign interests; and may pose threat of an onslaught 
on our social and cultural value systems. While the last  concern  would   be  
equally  applicable  to  all  the  foreign   content 
232 

[9 May, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
telecasting channels, the other concerns are valid largely for news and current 
affairs only. Arguably, therefore, the potential for mischief against safety and 
security of the State is more with a channel, which is largely dedicated to 
"News and Current Affairs Programmes" than others. 
Against this background, the guidelines for uplinking of foreign-
owned news channels have been reviewed in March, 2003. The revised 
guidelines permit foreign equity holding in the applicant-company upto 26 per 
cent of the total paid-up capital and require the company to be registered 
under the Companies Act, 1956 and the majority of Directors, CEOs and the 
News Editors to be "Resident Indians'.

world all these years. That is why I say that the Government should act with

269 

RAJYA SABHA [9 May, 2003] 
STATEMENT BY MINISTER 
Successful launch of second test flight of Geo-synchronous Satellite Launch 
Vehicle, GSLV - D2 from Sriharikota 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING, THE 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND 
PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
DEPARTMENT OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND DEPARTMENT OF SPACE (SHRI 
SATYABRAT MOOKHERJEE): Madam, I am happy to inform this august 
House that the second test flight of GSLV-D2 was successfully carried out 
from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, SHAR, Sriharikota on May 08, 2003. 
GSLV-D2 is a three-stage vehicle. It uses solid propellant first stage 
with four liquid strap-ons and a liquid propellant second stage. While the 
cryogenic third stage has been supplied by Russia, the control guidance and 
electronics for the stage have been designed, developed and implemented by 
ISRO scientists. The 49 metre tall technologically complex GSLV-D2, weighing 
400 tonnes, lifted off at 4.58 pm carrying GSAT-2 Satellite. After a perfect 
count down and about 17 minutes of smooth flight, GSAT-2 spacecraft was 
successfully placed into its intended orbit. GSLV-D2 has significantly 
demonstrated a payload capability of 1825 kg., which is about 300 kg. more 
than what was launched in the first flight. This was made possible by 
improvements such as the use of higher pressure engines for strap-ons, 
introduction of improved propellant loading for the core solid stage and 
optimisation of structural elements. This successful GSLV-D2 flight has 
validated the various technologies demonstrated during the first flight as well 
as improvements made for the second flight. 
The first signals acquired from the GSAT-2 satellite indicate normal 
health of the satellite. GSAT-2 will be raised to its final geo-synchronous orbit 
in the coming days followed by deployment of its solar arrays and antennae. 
The satellite, in addition to carrying transponders for communication and 
mobile satellite services, has four scientific experiments. 
With this successful flight of GSLV-D2, the payload capability has 
been established for launching operational communication satellites of 2000 
kg. class. Accomplishment of this technologically-challenging mission is the 
culmination of efforts of ISRO Centres supported by industries and academic 
institutions in India.

[9 May. 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
Madam, through you, I request this august House to join me in 
congratulating ISRO and other participants associated with the successful 
launch of GSLV-D2.

just take one minute. Multiple orbit raising operations are planned for GSAT-2 
satellite to raise its current geo-synchronous transfer orbit. The first of these 
orbit raising operations was successfully carried out at 8.45 this morning by 
firing 440 Newton Liquid Apogee Motor on board the satellite for a duration of 47 
minutes and 30 seconds. The health of the satellite is normal. Thank you.

Chairman, Sir, now that this Session is coming to an end, I take this 
opportunity to thank you, the Deputy Chairman, the Leader of the House, the 
leaders of all other political parties, for the smooth functioning of this 
284 

[9 May, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
House, which has, undoubtedly, enhanced the prestige and dignity of this 
House. 
Sir, this was a momentous Session and, as a responsible Opposition 
party, we have co-operated in the passage of the important financial 
legislation. But that does not mean that we do not have worries about the 
current state of our economy, or, the way it is being managed. We have grave 
worries about the fiscal situation in our country and also the overall economic 
condition, particularly with regard to the state of agriculture, the near neglect of 
public investment in agriculture. And, in the coming months, in particular, the 
problems that are going to be faced by the farmers, who are engaged in the 
growing of sugarcane, -tobacco and related commodities. These are the 
issues, I hope, on which the Government will pay attention to a much greater 
degree than it has paid in the past. Whatever be the state of monsoon, the 
next few months are going to be very hot for those States which are reeling 
under the impact of drought. I sincerely hope that the Government of India will 
come to the rescue of all those States which are coping with this menace of 
drought with great difficulty. Sir, we had wanted discussions on a number of 
other issues, but because of shortage of time we were not able to discuss 
those matters. We had read, with great concern, about the goings on in the 
DDA -- the scandals, which had come to notice. If time had permitted, we 
would have liked to discuss this matter also. Also, Sir, we know to great regret 
that while those involved in the Tehelka scam have not been punished, but the 
journalists, who exposed this sorry episode, have been penalised. 
Unfortunately, we were not able to discuss these matters. And, I do hope that 
as the House meets again in the Monsoon Session, some of these issues 
would engage our attention. 
Sir, with these words, I, once again, express to you, to the hon. 
Deputy Chairperson, the Panel of Vice-Chairmen, to the distinguished 
Secretary-General and his staff, and, above all, the Leader of the House and 
the hon. Minister for Parliamentary Affairs for all the cooperation that we have 
received from them, which facilitated greatly the smooth and orderly 
functioning of this House.

The House met at eleven of the clock, 
MR. CHAIRMAN in the Chair. 
(The National Anthem "Jana Gana Mana" was clayed) 
OBITUARY REFERENCES 
MR. CHAIRMAN : Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to 
the passing away of Shri Kishori Ram,  a former Member, Shri Korambayil 
Ahammed Haji, a sitting Member, Sh ri Pasumpon Tha Kiruttinan, Shri 
Indradeep Sinha, former Members, Shri Bhagatram Manhar, a sitting 
Member, Shrimati Premilabai Dajisaheb Chavan, a former Member of this 
House. 
Shri Kishori Ram passed away on the 4th February, 2003, at the age 
of 83 years. 
Born at Village Chakand,  District Gaya, Bihar in January,  1921, 
Shri Kishori Ram had his education  at vldwat Sahitya Sammelan, Aligarh. A 
businessman by profession, Shri Kishori Ram was associated with various 
social and welfare organisations.   He devoted his life for the   uplift of tne 
downtrodden. 
Shri Kishori Ram represented the State of Bihar in this House for 
two consecutive terms from April, 1952 to April, 1956 and again from April, 
1956 to April, 1962. 
In the passing away of Shri Kishori Ram the country has lost a 
noted social worker. 
Shri Korambayil Ahammed Haji passed away on the 12th May, 
2003, at the age of 72 years. 
Born at Manjeri, Kerala in June, 1931, Shri Haji had his education at 
Government Boys High School, Manjeri. A Businessman and Planter by 
profession, Shri Haji wa s associated with vari ous social, cultural and 
philanthropic activities. He served as the Director, Kerala Tourism 
Development Corporation. Shri Haji was a sports lover.   He was the founder 
1 

RAJYA SABHA [21 July, 2003] 
President of the Malappuram District Football Association and had also 
served as the Vice-President of the Kerala Football Association. From 1998 
till his death, Shri Haji served as the General Secretary of the Indian Union 
Muslim League, Kerala. 
Shri Korambayil Ahammed Haji star ted his legislative career as a 
Member of the Kerala Legislative Assembly in 1977 and remained its 
Member till 1991. Shri Haji was also elected, Deputy Speaker, Kerala 
Legislative Assembly in 1990. He represented the State of Kerala in this 
House from April, 1998 till his death. 
In the passing away of Shri Korambayil Ahammed Haji, the country 
has lost a noted social worker and a distinguished Parliamentarian. 
Shri Pasumpon Tha Kiruttinan passed away on the 20th of May, 
2003, at the age of 66 years under tragic circumstances. 
Born at village Kombukkaranendal, Tamil Nadu in May, 1937, Shri 
Kiruttinan had his education at Raja Dorai Singam Memorial College, 
Sivaganga and Pachaiyappa's College, Chennai. 
An Agriculturist by vocation, Shri Kiruttinan was an active social 
and political worker. He started social work as the Secretary of Red Cross 
Society at his native village and Kalai Valrchai Kazhagam, which does social 
work and educates the people thro ugh social dramas and cultural 
programmes. Shri Kiruttinan took keen interest in serving the poor, villagers, 
illiterates and people belonging to the lowest strata of society, including 
Harijans and those belonging to back ward classes. Shri Kiruttinan was 
arrested several times in connection with various agitations in favour of the 
people of Tamil Nadu. He was Chairman of the Panchayat Union, 
Manamadurai from 1970 to 1976 and President of the VillagePanchayat, 
Theethanpettai from 1970 to 1976. 
Shri Pasumpon Tha Kiruttinan starte d his distinguished legislative 
career with the membership of the Fourth Lok Sabha. He was re-elected to 
the Fifth Lok Sabha. Shri Kiruttinan represented the State of Tamil Nadu in 
this House from March, 1989 to April, 1990 and again from April, 1990 to 
April, 1996. Thereafter, he was elect ed to the Tamil Nadu Legislative 
Assembly in the year 1996 and remained a Member of that House till 2001. 
Shri Kiruttinan also served as the Minister of State Highways and Port in the 
Government of Tamil Nadu from 1998 to 2001. 
2 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

[21 July. 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
A widely travelled person, Shri Kiruttinan was member of the 
delegation to U.N.O. in the year 1990. He was also a member of the 
Parliamentary Delegation to  West Germany in the year 1972. 
In the passing away of Shri Pasumpon Tha Kiruttinan, the country 
has lost a distinguished social worker and a noted Parliamentarian. 
Shri Indradeep Sinha passed away on the 9th of June, 2003. at the 
age of 89 years following cardiac arrest. 
Born at Shakara village in Siwan District of Bihar in July, 1914, Shri 
Sinha had his education at Shakara, Dindayalpur, Maharajganj, Goreakothi 
and Patna. 
A lecturer and journalist by vocation, Shri Sinha was Secretary of 
the Bihar State Council of the Communi st Party of India from 1962 to 1967 
and had served as the General Secretar y of the All-India Kisan Sabha since 
1973 till late nineties. Shri Sinha was also editor of the 'Hunkar', 'Janasakti' 
and 'New Age' weeklies. 
Shri Indradeep Sinha started his legislative career with the 
Membership of the Bihar Legislative Co uncil, where he was a Member from 
1964 to 1974. He also served as the Minister of Revenue in the United Front 
Government of Bihar from 1967 to 1968. As Revenue Minister, he took 
several initiatives to amel iorate the condition of the poor and downtrodden 
classes and took steps for distribution of land to the landless in the State. Shri 
Sinha represented the State of Bihar in this House for two terms from April, 
1974 to April, 1980 and again from July, 1980 to July. 1986. 
In the passing away of Shri Indradeep Sinha, the country has lost a 
veteran Parliamentarian, a crusader for the common man's cause and an able 
administrator 
Shri Bhagatram Manhar passed away on the 19th June 2003, at the 
age of 65 years, following cardiac arrest. 
Born at Village Bhikhampura, District Raigarh, Chhattisgarh in 
October, 1938, Shri Manhar had done his graduation from the College of 
Agriculture, Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. An Agriculturist by vocation, Shri 
Manhar was associated with trade union activities. He worked closely with 
coalmines workers as patron of th e Rashtriya Koyala Khadan Mazdoor 
Sangh of the South-Eastern Coal Field.   He also worked for the welfare of 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [21 July, 2003] 
the  disadvantaged  sections of society.  Shri  Mannar served  as  Director, 
Tourism of the Chhattisgarh State. 
Shri Manhar began his legislative career with the membership of the 
Fifth Lok Sabha. He represented the State of Madhya Pradesh in this House 
for two consecutive terms from April 1978 to April, 1990. He was again 
elected to represent the State of Madhy a Pradesh in April, 2000. Consequent 
upon the creation of the State of Chhattisgarh, he represented that State from 
November, 2000 till his death. 
In the passing away of Shri Bhagat ram Manhar, the country has lost 
an able Parliamentarian who took keen interest in the proceedings of the 
House. 
Shrimati Premilabai Dajisaheb Chavan, passed away on the 8th 
July. 2003. at the age of 86 years. 
Born at Baroda in July, 1918 Shrimati Chavan had her education at 
Indore and Mumbai. A teacher by voca tion, Shrimati Chavan was an active 
social and political worker. She devoted  her life for the cause of women, 
sports and rural development. Shrimati Chavan was founder President of the 
All India Women's Cricket Association. She was also President of the Indian 
Business and Professional Women's Association. 
Shrimati Chavan had a long and distinguished legislative career. She 
was Member of the Fifth, Sixth, Eighth and Ninth Lok Sabha. She 
represented the State of Maharashtra in this House from July, 1980 to 
December, 1984. 
In the passing away of Shrimati Chavan the country has lost an 
eminent social worker and a distinguished Parliamentarian. 
We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri Kishori Ram, Shri 
Korambayil Ahammed Haji, Shri Pasu mpon Tha Kiruttinan, Shri Indradeep 
Sinha, Shri Bhagatram Manhar,   Shrimati Premilabai Dajisaheb Chavan .

within ten minutes of the train leaving the Ludhiana station and three coaches

WRITTEN ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS 
Disappearance of listed BSE companies 
*21.     SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: 
SHRI JIBON ROY: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that at least 2750 companies of 
the 5651 listed on the BSE were not available for trading and have gone 
missing with around Rs. 10,000 crore invested in these companies by 
millions of investors; 
(b) if so, how many of them have been officially declared as 
'disappeared' and the total amount of investors' money involved therein; 
and 
(c) what steps are being taken to ensure that the listed companies 
do not play 'Loot and Scoot' game with investors' money? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI JASWANT SINGH): (a) to (c) 
No, Sir. However, the Central Coordination and Monitoring Committee of 
Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Department of Company 
Affairs has informed that of the 7050 issues during the period 1992-98, 185 
companies could be identified as 'vanishing companies'. In these companies, 
the total monetary exposure involved is approximately Rs. 1150 crores. Of 
these companies, the total monetary exposure involved is approximately Rs. 
1150 crores. Of these 185 companies, 82 with total issue size (amount 
involved) of approximately Rs. 600 crores responded to the notices issued by 
SEBI and have, therefore, been cl assified as 'resurfaced vanishing 
companies'. The Department of Company Affairs has taken action including 
filing

prosecutions against companies under sections 62/63, 68 and 628 of the 
Companies Act, 1956. SEBI has debarred 93 companies and 351 directors 
under section 11B of the SEBI Act 1992 prohibiting them from associating in 
any way with the capital market activities.

SHRI R. P. GOENKA:

Action on Tarapore Committee Report 
*23.     SHRI MANOJ BHATTACHARYA: 
SHRI AIMADUDDIN AHMAD KHAN (DURRU): 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have taken any follow-up action with regard to the 
officials indicted by the Tarapore Comm ittee in January, 2002 In the U.T.I, 
scam; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(c) by when action is likely to be taken in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI JASWANT SINGH): (a) to (c) 
After detailed audit, and as recommended by the Tarapore Committee, 19 
cases were referred to the Advisory Board for Banking, Commercial and 
Financial Frauds (ABBCFF); which is a pre-investigative body under the 
Central Vigilance Commission. As the transactions/investment 
4 

[22 July, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
decisions commented upon by the Tarapo re Committee are essentially capital 
market related transactions, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) 
is the regulator in this regard. Therefore, the Government, in consultation with 
SEBI have referred 89 cases for inquiry by them (SEBI). 
In addition based on the recommendation of the Tarapore Committee, a 
departmental enquiry against officials of UTI was conducted, consequentially 
a former ED indicted, against whom a complaint was then lodged with the 
CBl.Two additional cases, inquired intern ally by the UTI, have also been 
lodged with the CBI.

Relevant Extracts from the minutes of the meeting of the appointments boards 
held in RBI, New Delhi on 11th October, 2000 
Agenda Item No. 2 
Procedure for appointment of whole time Directors in Public Sector 
Banks 
The Appointments Boar d recognized the need  for providing for a 
reasonable tenure for Whole Time Direct ors in Public Sector Banks in order 
to ensure that the bank gets the benefit of continuity in leadership in an era of 
increasing competition along with a fair method of selection based on merit 
with due consideration to seniority, for maintaining the morale and 
motivation of employees. The issue of re sidual service for Chief Executive in 
an institution matters a lot, as a Chief Executive with very short tenure implies 
lack of long-term commitment and vision and gaps in formulation and 
implementation of the long-term policy for the organisation. It was also felt 
that the whole issue of Co rporation Governance, which inter alia prescribes 
autonomy with accountability of the top management necessarily demands a 
minimum reasonable tenure for Chief Executives, which will avoid 
uncertainty and ensure continuity of policy. 
The Appointments Board also noted that the introduction of a procedure 
prescribing minimum tenure for appointment of whole time director will give 
rise to super-session of a few persons with excellent 
8 

[22 July, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
record for the top position on ground of their residual service being less than 
the minimum prescribed. However, the situation of super-session of otherwise 
qualified and competent persons will emerge at any time, when a transition 
from merit-cum-seniority procedure to tenure-oriented procedure is made. It 
was recognized that this may create resentment among some persons and may 
impinge on building organisational teams at higher levels. 
The Appointments Boar d also recognized th at the procedure for 
prescribing minimum tenure for whole time directors in State Bank of India 
(SBI) keeping in view its special stat us, large size and trained and skilled 
manpower, may be somewhat different from the one which may be followed 
for the nationalised banks. Keeping in view the constraints of public sector 
character of these banks and the existing guidelines of Department of 
Personnel and Training, the Appointments Board suggested that the following 
system may be followed by the Board while considering candidates for 
appointment as whole-time directors on the Boards of public sector banks:— 
(a) For Chairman and Managing Direct or of SBI—a minimum residual 
service of two years from the date the vacancy arises. 
(b) For Managing Director of SBI—a minimum residual service of one 
year from the date the vacancy arises. 
(c) For Chairman and Managing Director of Nationalised Banks— All 
persons with minimum residual service of two years as on 1st April of 
the financial year in which vacancy arises will be considered. 
However, it should be kept in view that the person who is 
recommended for a particular nationalised bank should as far as 
feasible, have at least two years of service in the concerned bank. 
(d) For executive Directors of Nationalised Banks—A minimum residual 
service of two years as on 1st April ot the concerned financial year 
shall be considered for the purpose of calling people for interview…"

Concessional airfares to holiday travellers 
148.    DR. AKHILESH DAS: 
SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Indian Airlines, Air Alliance and Air India announced 
concessional air fares for holiday travellers this year; 
(b) if so, the details of the concessions and the fares offered; and 
(c) how far (giving percentage) they were successful in capturing/ 
cornering the holiday-air-travel fares collections vis-a-vis private air 
operators? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL 
AVIATION (SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDI): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Air India has 
introduced off-season holiday packages to boost inbound tourists to India as 
well as to improve seat factors on the Gulf/India and UK/ Europe/India routes 
during the lean season. Air-India holiday packages were introduced in the Gulf 
and Middle East from March 15, 2003 and are valid till September 30, 2003 
with a black out period from June 25, 2003 to July 15, 2003. These holiday 
packages cover two destinations viz, Goa and Kerala. The duration of holiday 
packages for Goa is 3 nights 4 days and for Kerala is 6 nights 7 days. The 
special fares for these holiday packag es are approximately 20% lower than 
the current 
29 

RAJYA SABHA [22 July, 2003] 
market fares applicable from these markets, namely, UAE, Oman, Qatar, 
Bahrain, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia. Air-India has not introduced its own 
holiday packages from UK and Europe. However, the Indian Association of Tour 
Operators (IATO) has been offered fares for putting together their own 
holiday packages to India from UK and Europe. The fare given to IATO is at 
the same level as is available with tour operators/Travel agents in Europe. The 
fares given to IATO are valid only during specified lean period in the specific 
route i.e. UK/India/UK and Europe/India/ Europe, the period specified is 19th 
August, 2003 to 30th September, 2003 and 15th March, 2004 to 30th June, 
2004. The fares cannot be sold separately, i.e. without any land arrangements 
and can only be used as part of regular brochure tour package. Moreover, the 
ticket on these fares can only be issued in the country of origin of travel and by 
a licensed tour operator in that country. 
(c) Although the Air India holiday packages were welcomed by the 
tourism trade, their launch unfortunately coincided with the build up of 
tensions in the Gulf region. Consequently passengers from the Gulf countries 
were disinclined to undertake leisure travel. As a result, these holiday packages 
were unable to attract substantial number of tourists due to the uncertain 
situation. 
As regards Indian Airlines, they have not announced any special Air 
fares for holiday travellers this year but has ongoing concessional airfares 
and holiday packages which were introduced in the past and are continuing.
